title: No Misuse of IndiaAI Support by Sarvam, IT Secretary Krishnan Says
excerpt: MeitY Secretary S Krishnan defended Sarvam AI's Token Factory, which hosts Chinese open-weight models alongside its own, saying the commercial service does not contradict its IndiaAI-backed sovereign model work.
body:
• MeitY Secretary S Krishnan said on Wednesday that the government sees no misuse of IndiaAI Mission support in Sarvam AI's commercial Token Factory service.
  • Token Factory, launched November 16, serves Sarvam's own models alongside open-weight models including DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM through a single API, on GPU clusters located in India.
  • Sarvam says Token Factory runs on privately procured GPUs, not the subsidised IndiaAI compute it used to train its 105-billion-parameter model.
  • Krishnan said the government is also supporting Sarvam's work towards a trillion-parameter model, and will work on a scheme to support AI inference.

The government has publicly backed Sarvam AI in the row over the Bengaluru startup hosting Chinese-developed AI models on its new commercial platform. Speaking on Wednesday, on the sidelines of a text-to-speech model launch by Chariot AI, Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) Secretary S Krishnan said the government sees no contradiction between Sarvam's indigenous model development, supported by the IndiaAI Mission, and its new offering of open-source-based models to enterprises — and no misuse of the support it received.

"I think based on what Sarvam has told us, based on the experience that people have, we do not see any misuse of the support which the India AI mission has provided to Sarvam in the service that they are now offering."

— S Krishnan, MeitY Secretary

What the controversy is about

Sarvam launched Token Factory on November 16, describing it as an inference stack to serve its own models and leading open-weight models from GPU clusters located in India, through a single API for enterprises. Social media users noted that six of the models listed are Chinese, including DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM, and only one is Sarvam's own 105B model, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. Critics questioned how hosting Chinese models fits with India's sovereign AI push, especially for a startup that has had government support.

Sarvam's answer is that the two activities run on different money. The company has said Token Factory relies strictly on privately procured GPUs and not state-sponsored subsidies, and that the service will create a commercial opportunity for the company, reduce latency and trim India's dependence on overseas token platforms, according to Inc42. Krishnan echoed the distinction: Sarvam's work on the indigenous model is different from its inference platform, and, he said, "AI companies also require a revenue model."

What IndiaAI support actually funded

Krishnan said Sarvam has received support from the IndiaAI Mission to train AI models with 105 billion parameters and a few other models. He said Sarvam had informed the ministry it planned to create a harness with a number of open-source and open-weight models, including its own, to provide AI services from India to Indian consumers and customers. He added that he has received feedback from start-ups and entities that have used Sarvam's services that their performance is as good as any other frontier model.

What happens next

Two government moves follow from Krishnan's remarks. First, the government is also supporting Sarvam's work towards a trillion-parameter model. Second, MeitY will work on a scheme to support inference by AI models — the cost-intensive step of actually serving a trained model to users — which Krishnan described as crucial to the development of a full-fledged AI platform. No budget or timeline for the inference scheme was announced. Since the Token Factory launch, Sarvam has also rolled out an upgraded Sarvam-105B checkpoint and a dictation API for English and 22 Indian languages—releases the company points to as evidence that its commercial services have not diluted its core model work.
